title: Mental math for beginners: make numbers feel easier

lessons.objective: Split an addition so the first step reaches ten.
Move a few counters and see why an awkward sum gets easier.
Double one factor and halve the other without changing the product.
Double first, divide by ten, and check the result—even with decimals.
Count ten bags of sweets, then add the last bag.
See what half, a quarter and ten percent look like.
Calculate a percentage change using the correct starting amount and explain why equal percentage decreases and increases do not cancel.

sources.name: OpenStax — Prealgebra 2e: General Applications of Percent
University of Cambridge NRICH — Dating Made Easier

glossary.definition: The total when you add amounts together.
A share described as an amount out of every hundred.
The difference between new and original amounts expressed as a percentage of a positive original amount.

outcomes: Keep a product unchanged by doubling and halving.
Divide by five and explain why doubling helps.
Build simple percentages from familiar parts.
Use the correct starting amount for each percentage change and distinguish a fall from the rise needed to reverse it.
description: Seven short mental math lessons: make friendly numbers, round, double, divide and build percentages, then discover why equal percentage changes do not cancel. Optional quizzes included.
introduction:
Make ten, adjust a rounded number, double and halve, then try a few useful multiplication and division shortcuts. Build percentages from smaller shares before exploring a backpack price that drops and rises by the same percentage.

Each short lesson adds one idea. Read at your own pace and check the everyday examples; the quiz is optional.
prerequisites: Comfort with basic addition, subtraction and multiplication.
